title: Economic activity grows 12.8% in October, fastest in three years, ICRA index shows
dek: The rating agency's monitor of 16 indicators points to strong construction and festive demand, but ICRA says a low base flattered the number and expects growth to cool in November.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's economic activity grew 12.8% year on year in October, the fastest pace in three years, according to the ICRA Business Activity Monitor, a composite of 16 high-frequency indicators compiled by the rating agency ICRA. Growth was up from 12.1% in September and was the fifth month running of double-digit expansion.

ICRA said part of the jump reflected a low base: last October's activity was depressed by unseasonal rain and by the timing of festivals. It expects growth to cool in November, when Dhanteras and Diwali fell this year and holidays were more numerous, and said an average of the October and November readings would give a better picture of festive-season demand.

## What drove October

Eleven of the 16 indicators improved year on year compared with September, ICRA said. On a month-on-month basis the index rose 7.1% in October, after 1.6% in September, according to reports of the release.

Construction-linked indicators were strong. Cement output grew 15.4%, up from 10.1% in September, and ICRA said the growth in cement and steel output indicated that construction activity remained healthy, according to reports.

Factory output of vehicles surged ahead of the festive season. Two-wheeler production grew 29.2%, up from 11.3%, and passenger vehicle production rose 26.4%, up from 16.2%. Vehicle registrations, which measure sales to customers, fell 23.3% after rising 33.4% in September, because October 2025 had been inflated by the festive rush that followed the GST rate cuts of late September last year.

## The festive season in numbers

Early November data point to strong retail demand. Average daily vehicle registrations from 1 to 21 November rose about 29% year on year to 143,100 units, according to ICRA. Automobile retail sales over the 42-day festive period from 11 October to 21 November reached about 55 lakh units, 2.2% more than last year's record festive season, according to dealers' association data cited by ICRA.

Electricity demand growth slowed to 11.8% so far in November, from 21% in October, and rabi sowing was 11% lower than a year earlier as of 13 November, reports said.

The labour market also improved. The unemployment rate fell to 4.9% in October from 5% in September, its lowest in eight months, according to the official monthly labour force survey. The labour force participation rate rose to 55.7% and the worker-population ratio rose 30 basis points to 53%, helped by more women and rural workers in jobs, according to reports.

## Why it matters

The ICRA index is watched as an early read on the economy before official data arrive. The government's estimate of GDP growth for July-September, the second quarter of 2026-27, is due at the end of November. A strong October would support the view that domestic demand is holding up even as the United States prepares new tariffs on Indian goods.

## What happens next

ICRA expects core sector growth to ease to the mid-single digits in November. The second-quarter GDP estimate and the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decision in December will show whether the October surge carried into the rest of the quarter.
